posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
If I were going to square "only 18 shards" with "copies of people everywhere", I would assume that Oblivaeon Shards are also kind of singular things. The shard that empowers Captain Cosmic is the same shard across all timelines; when it broke, a whole mess of timelines got access to it. 

 

If that's the case, it would make sense that there are at least seven active shards in the main Sentinels timeline despite only 18 people across all of history and all the Mutiverse injuring him. Those were injuries by realities close enough to the "main" one to appear there.

posts.name: X-metal
posts.cooked: Off topic but technically not: who’s excited for Xtreme-verse today.

Accident is a category of superpower source that I’m a little tired of; if I were GMing a game of some superhero RPG, I would firmly discourage players from picking this origin. If they have an Absolute Zero level of backstory that makes it thematically fitting, I’d bend that rule, but if they were building Tachyon, I’d firmly push them out of the origin story being “hit by lightning while juggling weird chemicals” and toward something less, well, Golden Age levels of contrivance.

Higher Power for Ra I would disapprove of, but it would work for the original Anubis, since he’s never yet had his power stored in a relic which a normal person picks up and is transformed by.

About energy, KNYFE’s blades are obviously mostly manifested kinetic energy; it’s right there in the acronym, Kinetic Neutralizer. They glow for comic book reasons, which specifically contradicts the physics of our world (in real life, a lightsaber would be weaker than an otherwise identical weapon that shed no light, because glowing means radiating light energy and thus wasting potential destructive yield), and this is enough to let Dawn control them, but I wouldn’t say they’re primarily like laser blades. As for doctor Medico, we know he has a degree of solidity and mass, at least as much as like a Star Trek hologram, so he may be like 99.99% pure life energy, but there’s clearly some kind of particle cloud serving as his body, he can’t pass through a completely solid wall or the like, and when he’s KOed or worse, he collapsed into a pile of powder.

PS, I like that Medico makes “skin to skin” contact with an Oblivion Shard.

Singular for a Host spirit should never be “a Host”, btw. “The Host” is a collective term for the whole throng of such entities; calling one “a Host” is like calling a person “a crowd”. I’ll forgive Christopher this slip of the tongue, since he’s talking at legendary speed, but I still have to pick the nits that can be picked.

MindWanderer:

I call baloney on the number of OblivAeon shards floating around out there. We only know of a few specific ones outside the six on core-Earth, but there are enough to infer more. In particular, every universe where there’s an alternate version of Captain Cosmic and Infinitor has one. That’s the Quando universe for sure, probably the Inverse Universe (though we’ll find out with the Inverse Prime Wardens episode which I’m sure will happen), and also the pun universes. The pun universes add up to a lot all by themselves, since we know that every “legal” pun corresponds to an actual character, and there are certainly pun universes beyond the three confirmed so far.

Alternate versions of Proletariat should also be based on shards (e.g. Everyman, probably), and we know there are other random ones, like Iron Legacy Parse, that Disparation writers probably tossed around without really keeping track.

I would say that the number of shards that {spoiler} broke off of OA is correct, but each such shard then exists at a random point in spacetime, and then whenever a new timeline splits off, that oblivion shard exists simultaneously in both timelines, with a set of coordinates in each one. Thusly, the Proletariat shard broke off “Blivs”, and let’s say it landed precisely five miles due west of the front door of the Kremlin. In every universe that has a Kremlin, that shard starts out at that position, but in the Inverted Universe, somebody at some point in history went to Russia, picked up that shard, and transported it to America so they could create The Every Man.

Even if the shard appears to be destroyed, it’s only destroying the physical object which represents the coordinate set of that shard in that universe. One such shard is in England, where it gets absorbed by Captain Cosmic and Infinitor; the shard still exists in every universe that doesn’t have any people in England, just sitting there untouched. When Plaything creates an ape body for Infinitor, a new coordinate is created for just the green half of that shard, and thus the shard reappears as if it was physical, but it’s still not the superdimensional crystal flesh of OA, just a “web link” that displays that object within a particular dimension.

Last but not least, my character is the Inversiverse Dante Serpenta, the hero Whitesnake, sworn enemy of the Northeast Sentinels before they gain Infinity Stones and become the Void Raid.
